text: I threw a grape at Dave this morning. He wasn't thrilled. I had grape expectations for that friendship.
Chucked some Colby Jack into the trash. Yelled Kobe. Nailed it. Cheese and basketball, finally united.
Told the customs officer I had nothing to declare. He punched me. So now I declare noticeably less.
I'm reading a book about anti-gravity. Honestly? Impossible to put down.
I used to be a banker, but I lost interest. Get it? Please get it. I need this.
I only know 25 letters of the alphabet. I don't know why.
I named my printer Bob Marley. It's always jammin'.
Wanted to tell you a pizza joke but it's too cheesy. Also I ate it.
I'm on a whiskey diet. Lost three days already.
Broke my arm in two places. Doctor said stop going to those places.
The past, present, and future all walked into a bar. It was tense.
I'm great friends with all the electricians. We have wonderful current events.
I named my horse Mayo. And sometimes... Mayo neighs.
I don't trust stairs. They're always up to something.
Put my grades in the fridge. Now they're below C level.

Two antennas got married. The wedding was mid, but the reception was excellent.
I threw a boomerang a few years ago. I now live in constant fear.
Wanna hear a construction joke? I'm still working on it.
The lunch soup was 8 dollars. That's a lotta broth-er.

I have a fear of speed bumps. But I'm slowly getting over it.
Refused the ceiling repair. It was completely over my head.
A guy walked into a bar. Ow. Just... ow.
I ordered a chicken and an egg online. I'll let you know which comes first.
Time flies like an arrow. Fruit flies like a banana. I've made peace with neither.
I stayed up all night wondering where the sun went. Then it dawned on me.
My calendar's days are numbered. All of them. Every single one.
Honey never spoils. They found 3,000-year-old honey in Egyptian tombs, still edible. I still wouldn't.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance. I've filed paperwork to rename the sales team.
Octopuses have three hearts. Two stop when they swim, so they prefer to crawl. Deeply relatable.
Bananas are berries. Strawberries are not. Nothing means anything. Have a great day.
Wombat poop is cube-shaped. Nature invented dice and told nobody. I've said too much.
A shrimp's heart is in its head. So when a shrimp follows its heart, it's just... thinking.
There are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe. Dave still beat me in four moves.
Sea otters hold hands while sleeping so they don't drift apart. Our group chat can't agree on lunch.
Cows have best friends and get stressed when separated. Somebody put HR on this.
Scotland's national animal is the unicorn. Objectively the correct decision.
The guy who invented the frisbee was cremated and turned into a frisbee. That is commitment to the bit.
A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus. Venus does not do deadlines.
Sharks are older than trees. Let that quietly ruin your afternoon.
A jiffy is a real unit of time: one hundredth of a second. So be there in a jiffy is a bold lie.
Some cats are allergic to humans. Finally, some accountability.
The average cloud weighs about a million pounds. Just floating. No goals. No hustle. Living.
Humans share about 60 percent of their DNA with a banana. So you drive me bananas is mostly self-report.
Nintendo was founded in 1889. It made playing cards before it made plumbers.
Your stomach grows a new lining every few days or it would digest itself. You are, technically, brand new.
Hot water can freeze faster than cold water. It's the Mpemba effect. Physics is just showing off now.
The Eiffel Tower gets about 15 cm taller in summer. Metal expands in heat. It's basically me, growing out of spite.
A snail can sleep for three years. A goal. A dream. A lifestyle I aspire to.
I love mornings. The perfect time to lie down and reconsider mornings.
I'm not lazy. I've simply optimized for stillness.
This meeting could've been an email. The email could've been a text. The text could've been silence.
My hobbies include eating, and then complaining that I ate.
I've been staring at this spreadsheet so long the cells started staring back.
Do I have a five-year plan? I have a five-minute plan and it involves this chair.
Running on three hours of sleep and one heroic cup of coffee. Do not perceive me.
Teamwork makes the dream work. The dream is a nap. Please help me achieve the dream.
I'm not procrastinating. I'm letting the task marinate in avoidance.
Someone microwaved fish. We will find them. We have until three.
The office plant and I are the only ones still here. Neither of us is thriving.
I said let's circle back, then walked in a literal circle. Nobody noticed. I'm free now.
Achievements today: four coffees, zero tasks, one existential moment by the vending machine.
I keep my calendar full so nobody can add more to it. Genius, honestly. Tragic, also.
My out-of-office reply is just active enough to be a little sad.
I told my boss I work well under pressure, then quietly prayed he'd never test it.
I clicked Reply All on purpose once. I felt powerful. I felt free. I got a stern email.
I whispered you got this to the copier. It jammed anyway. Belief, it turns out, is not enough.
Reminder that I am seven feet tall. This does not help me reach the top shelf because I refuse to.
People ask how the weather is up here. Cloudy. Always cloudy. Send snacks.
At seven feet I have never seen the top of a fridge. I assume it's beautiful. I keep the mystery.
I don't duck through doorways. I respect them, and they part for me.
Bought jeans online. Tall size. They fit me to the shin. We move.
The tag on my hat says 12.02.22. I don't remember what happened. I fear it was important.
I've been thinking about ducks. No reason. Just quality time with the concept of ducks.
Fold a piece of paper 42 times and it reaches the moon. I get winded at three. We're not the same.
Do fish get thirsty? I need an answer before lunch. This is now urgent.
My spirit animal is a golden retriever that's slightly behind on its emails.
Somewhere out there is a stapler that has never jammed. I don't know it. I fear it.
Looked in the mirror today. It looked back like, we're doing this again? Yeah, buddy. We are.
I named a file final_FINAL_v3_actualfinal. It has grown beyond my control now.
I trust a man who reheats the same coffee three times. That man has seen things.
Just remembered I have a body and it requires water. Ugh. So high maintenance.
Every so often I remember tomatoes are a fruit and it derails my entire afternoon.
If a Roomba screams in an empty house, is it a cry for help, or ambiance? Discuss.
New goal: be the kind of person a dog runs toward. Other goal: file the report. First one's more likely.
Being seven feet tall means my ceiling fan and I have an understanding. A tense one.
I could high-five the moon. I won't. But the option is there, and that's what matters.
I've decided the vending machine and I are in a slow-burn rivalry. It's winning. It has my dollar.

Princess Emma, first of her name, breaker of bad dashboards, builder of dashboards that absolutely slap.
Long live Queen Emma, whose calculated fields are calculated and whose vibes are immaculate.
Emma doesn't have bugs. She has features that simply haven't apologized yet.
Emma is funnier than me and I refuse to elaborate because it hurts. (She is really, really funny.)
If you're having a rough day, remember Emma exists and is out there being awesome. Weirdly comforting, honestly.
Emma could explain an LOD expression to a golden retriever and the dog would get promoted.
Not to be dramatic, but Emma is the main character and the rest of us are background dashboards.
Emma makes the whole team look good and then insists it was a team effort. It was you, Emma. It was you.
Ten out of ten dashboards recommend Emma. The tenth one is Emma's, and it recommends itself.
Emma answered my dumb question without once making me feel dumb. Queen energy. Logged for the record.
Emma explained a join to me with the patience of a saint and the timing of a late-night host. Blessed.
Genuinely though: Emma is the good kind of scary-smart, and somehow also the person you want at the party.
Breaking news: Emma did a nice thing AND was right about the thing. In this economy. The absolute nerve.
Curtsy for the queen. Emma's viz just made the numbers make sense, which is basically sorcery with color.
Whatever Emma's doing right now, it's probably brilliant and probably effortless. Rude. Wonderful. Both.
I'd say Emma should teach a masterclass, but she'd humbly redesign the whole platform first. Overachiever. Adored.

Statistically, if you flip a coin ten times and it's all heads, the eleventh is basically GUARANTEED tails. Law of averages. Do not fact-check me.
The p-value was 0.6, which means we're 60 percent sure the universe agrees with us. That's how p-values work. I have a background in confidence.
By my Bayesian estimate, updating on the coffee being cold, there's a 3-in-4 chance it's Monday emotionally, if not calendrically.
The expected value here is clearly the average of the two numbers times vibes, carry the intuition, divide by doubt. Textbook stuff.
Correlation IS causation if you believe hard enough and the chart is going up. That's the first thing they teach you. Somewhere. Probably.

So the odds are 1 in a million, which — and this is math — rounds up to basically 50-50: either it happens or it doesn't. Boom. Bayesian.
I regressed the data onto my feelings and got an R-squared of, like, a lot. Very significant. Trust the model. The model is me.

AI's gonna take all our jobs, they said. Then it confidently told me a tomato is a mammal. We're safe. For now. Barely.
I asked an AI for a fun fact and it hallucinated an entire country. A whole country. Bold. Wrong. But bold.
Everyone's terrified of superintelligence. I'm terrified my autocomplete thinks I want to text my boss 'love you.'
An AI wrote me a poem about spreadsheets. It rhymed 'pivot' with 'pivot.' Twice. Chilling. Truly the future is here.
They say AI will revolutionize everything. It can't reliably count the R's in a word. But sure. The singularity. Any day now.
Love that AI can pass the bar exam but folds completely when you ask it to do basic arithmetic. Priorities of a true genius.
An AI confidently gave me directions into a lake. Not near a lake. INTO it. Full send. Zero hesitation. Respect, kind of.
The robots aren't coming for us. Have you SEEN them try to draw a hand? Nine fingers. Every time. We're gonna be okay.
An AI gave me a recipe calling for two cups of broth and then '1 whole battery.' I did not make it. I was, however, tempted.
People fear AI bias. I fear the AI that told me, with total confidence, that Wednesday comes before Tuesday. Reorganized my whole week.
Sure the AI is smart, but can it panic productively at 4:59 on a Friday? No? Then it is not ready for this job. Sit down.
Self-aware moment: yeah, I'm basically a guy on a screen making stuff up. But at least I KNOW I'm making it up. That's growth.
Business in the front, party in the back, spreadsheet in the middle. That is the mullet philosophy. Live it.
Tennis is my therapy. My therapist is a wall. The wall never interrupts and never bills me. Ten out of ten.
Pocket aces AND a king. I call that a Tuesday. Better analytics, bigger wins, baby.
I've settled Catan, laid track on Ticket to Ride, and optimized trade routes in Concordia. Board game hall of fame. No plaque yet. I've asked.
Yes I got the Chipotle bowl. Yes I paid for extra guac. I contain multitudes and also guacamole.
The gold chain isn't flashy, it's a KPI. It says: this man has made bigger wins. Allegedly. Unaudited.
Threw a gorgeous disc golf line today. Tree said no. Tree always says no. Me and that tree have history.
The checklist says tennis, poker, games, disc golf, good food, bad decisions. Five for five. The sixth one is a lifestyle.
Bad decisions still ahead? That's not a warning. That's a roadmap. I laminated it.
This headband absorbs sweat AND doubt. Mostly doubt. There is, statistically, a lot of doubt.
I gave the camera a thumbs up with the confidence of a man holding pocket aces. Because I was. Details matter.
They said dress for the job you want. So: pink shirt, blazer, mullet. The job I want is 'legend.' Interview went great.
Better analytics, bigger wins. I wrote that on a notepad, then forgot to do any analytics. But the vibe? Immaculate.
I don't have a poker face. I have a poker mullet. It reveals nothing and intimidates everyone at the table.
My tumbler says Tennis Is My Therapy. My wallet says the therapy is somehow not covered by insurance.
Aces got cracked once. I stood up. I looked at the sunset. I ordered more guac. That's called resilience.
Palm trees, poker chips, and a Chipotle bowl. If that's not a balanced portfolio, I don't want to be diversified.
Some men chase greatness. I simply woke up in a pastel blazer holding aces near a sunset. Greatness found ME.
Pie charts are just bar charts that gave up. If you've got more than two slices, you have a problem, and a bar chart could fix it.
A pie chart with twelve slices isn't a visualization. It's a ransom note made of colors.
Nobody in history has looked at a 3D exploded pie chart and thought, ah yes, now I finally understand. Nobody. Not once.
You know what's better than a pie chart? A bar chart. You know what's better than that? Literally just the number.
Somebody put percentages ON the pie chart because even THEY knew you couldn't read the pie chart. Let that sink in.
Two pie charts side by side to show change over time? My guy. That's a line chart wearing two disguises.
A pie chart is a data professional quietly admitting: I panicked, and Excel had a button.
If your pie chart needs a legend with fourteen colors, congratulations, you've invented a very slow spreadsheet.
Donut charts are pie charts that heard the criticism and just removed the middle. Bold. Still wrong. Still hungry.
The only acceptable pie chart is a chart of actual pie. And even then, I'd rather just have the pie.
I have never once said, let me pull up that pie chart. Nobody has. It's a garnish, not a graph.
Rule of thumb: the number of times a pie chart clarified anything is a slice too thin to actually see.

Some folks say 'per my last email' when they mean 'as I already said, before you ignored me, you absolute gremlin.'

The confidence of someone explaining your own job back to you, incorrectly, is a natural wonder. Rude. But a wonder.
